It offers ample space and comfort, complemented by a strong feature set that includes ventilated seats, a panoramic sunroof, and a Bose sound system. Driving enthusiasts will appreciate the performance of the 1.5-litre turbo-petrol engine and the improved handling package offered by the N Line variants. Buyers focused on fuel economy can opt for the refined 1.5-litre petrol or diesel engines. It is hard to go wrong with the Creta, no matter what your needs are. And remember, there are electric variants too. Key SpecificationsHighlightsSpecs and FeaturesHyundai Creta priceCreta has 54 variants from ₹12.61L across 1.5L petrol, 1.5L diesel and 1.5L Turbo, in 6MT, iVT, 6AT and 7DCT. E (₹12.61L diesel / ₹10.91L petrol) is the safety base with 6 airbags, ESC, hill-start and all 4 disc brakes. EX (from ₹12.07L) adds the 20.32cm touchscreen with wireless CarPlay, auto headlamps and dual zone climate. EX(O) (from ₹13.14L) brings quad-beam LED headlamps and front parking sensors. S(O) (from ₹14.21L) steps up to voice panoramic sunroof, EPB and smart key push start. SX (from ₹15.04L) adds Bose 8-speaker audio, ventilated front seats, 17-inch alloys, surround view camera and Bluelink. King (from ₹17.28L) tops it off with Level 2 ADAS, 18-inch alloys and electric driver seat with memory. Most buyers land at SX MT (₹15.04L) — you get Bose audio, voice sunroof, ventilated seats, 17-inch alloys, surround view and 6 airbags standard, without paying ~₹2.23L extra for King's Level 2 ADAS
